CaptureStep.title: Capture Step
CaptureStep.description: One generic browser interaction performed before a screenshot is taken, used to drive an element into a non-rest state. Source-agnostic — the same shape applies to a reference page or a Storybook story.

selector.description: CSS selector the action targets. Required for click/hover/focus; omitted for a bare wait.

timeout.description: Milliseconds to let the UI settle after the action.

CaptureState.title: Capture State
CaptureState.description: A named interaction condition under which a screenshot is captured. `rest` is the implicit default (no steps — the element as first rendered); any other state is reached by running `steps` in order. Names are generic UI conditions (rest, expanded, open, …), never component- or site-specific.

name.description: Generic state name. `rest` is reserved for the default un-interacted state.

steps.description: Interactions to reach this state from rest. Empty for `rest`.

items.title: Capture Step
items.description: One generic browser interaction performed before a screenshot is taken, used to drive an element into a non-rest state. Source-agnostic — the same shape applies to a reference page or a Storybook story.

selector.description: CSS selector the action targets. Required for click/hover/focus; omitted for a bare wait.

timeout.description: Milliseconds to let the UI settle after the action.

BreakpointId.description: Viewport breakpoint identifier from `design-tokens.yml` (sm, md, lg, xl, ...). Determines the viewport width for capture/verify operations.

ElementId.description: Stable label for the comparison subject, used in filenames and scores. Name the rendered surface, not the capture area: entity stories use `entity-<entity_type>-<bundle>-<view_mode>` (for example `entity-paragraph-signage-full`, where `full` is the view mode), scene regions use names such as `scene-header` or `scene-footer`, and components use `component-<name>`. Use `selector: ""` to capture the isolated story root; do not encode that capture mode as `id: full`. A trailing `full` in an entity id is valid when it is the entity view mode.

Screenshot.title: Screenshot
Screenshot.description: Atomic capture descriptor — one rendered image, identical shape on the reference (baseline) and story sides. Identity is (element, state, breakpoint). The on-disk filename is derived: `<breakpoint>--<element>--<state>.png`.

element.description: Stable label for the comparison subject, used in filenames and scores. Name the rendered surface, not the capture area: entity stories use `entity-<entity_type>-<bundle>-<view_mode>` (for example `entity-paragraph-signage-full`, where `full` is the view mode), scene regions use names such as `scene-header` or `scene-footer`, and components use `component-<name>`. Use `selector: ""` to capture the isolated story root; do not encode that capture mode as `id: full`. A trailing `full` in an entity id is valid when it is the entity view mode.

breakpoint.description: Viewport breakpoint identifier from `design-tokens.yml` (sm, md, lg, xl, ...). Determines the viewport width for capture/verify operations.

threshold.description: Maximum differing-pixel ratio accepted by this planned check; set during intake.

selector.description: CSS selector for THIS side's capture; "" ⇒ isolated root / full. Reference side uses the Reference element's selector, story side uses the StoryMeta element's selector — context (which meta) disambiguates.

Overview.title: Overview
Overview.description: Full-page reference overview at one viewport — a human-facing at-a-glance capture of the whole reference, distinct from the element compare matrix (`Screenshot`) and never a compare cell. The on-disk filename is derived: `overview--<viewport>--<breakpoint>.png`. Two are captured per reference: the narrowest defined breakpoint (mobile) and the widest (desktop).

viewport.description: `mobile` = narrowest defined breakpoint, `desktop` = widest defined breakpoint. Names the human-facing viewport, not the capture area.

breakpoint.description: Viewport breakpoint identifier from `design-tokens.yml` (sm, md, lg, xl, ...). Determines the viewport width for capture/verify operations.

Element.title: Element
Element.description: Named comparison subject. The `id` identifies the rendered surface (`entity-paragraph-signage-full`, `scene-header`, `component-card`), not the capture-area label. Carries this side's selector plus the state × breakpoint matrix that materializes into Screenshots.

id.description: Stable label for the comparison subject, used in filenames and scores. Name the rendered surface, not the capture area: entity stories use `entity-<entity_type>-<bundle>-<view_mode>` (for example `entity-paragraph-signage-full`, where `full` is the view mode), scene regions use names such as `scene-header` or `scene-footer`, and components use `component-<name>`. Use `selector: ""` to capture the isolated story root; do not encode that capture mode as `id: full`. A trailing `full` in an entity id is valid when it is the entity view mode.

reference_selector.description: Optional selector for the reference (baseline) side when it differs from the candidate `selector`. Used when the two sides isolate the same subject with different selectors — e.g. sync-verify, where `selector` isolates the subject in the backend render and `reference_selector` isolates the Storybook story root. Defaults to `selector` when omitted.

items.title: Capture Step
items.description: One generic browser interaction performed before a screenshot is taken, used to drive an element into a non-rest state. Source-agnostic — the same shape applies to a reference page or a Storybook story.

selector.description: CSS selector the action targets. Required for click/hover/focus; omitted for a bare wait.

timeout.description: Milliseconds to let the UI settle after the action.

items.description: Viewport breakpoint identifier from `design-tokens.yml` (sm, md, lg, xl, ...). Determines the viewport width for capture/verify operations.

Reference.title: Captured observation metadata
Reference.description: One source-neutral snapshot shared by reference and actual Storybook capture. Publication identity is supplied by the CLI binding manifest.

elements.description: Selected subjects with their observed state and view coverage.

prelude_digest.description: SHA-256 of the prelude module that prepared every pass of this revision. Absent when the capture used no prelude. Fixing it here means a later prelude edit cannot silently redefine what was observed.

SourceDump.title: Stored source extract
SourceDump.description: One browser dump for one state of a capture revision (`extract--<state>.json`): one page load, in one session, at that state. Agents consume it through `reference save` stdout, `reference inspect` and `reference query`, never by opening the file. Walker-specific extra keys on the dump object are allowed.

source_ref.description: Observed source identity, typically the URL.

nodes.description: Observed nodes with native locators, boxes and styles. Extra walker keys are allowed.

items.description: One captured node. Keys include id, kind, locator, box and style.

ReferenceFolder.description: Path to a scene's verification material — contains one source dump per declared state (`extract--<state>.json`), `meta.yml`, and one screenshot per view/element/state cell, named `<view>--<element>--<state>.png`. The leading segment is the view id the metadata declares; a view carries a breakpoint only where that mapping is established, and the file name stays on the view.

CompareArtifact.title: Compare Artifact
CompareArtifact.description: Structured result of one screenshot compare check. One item is emitted per `(breakpoint, element, state)` triple so outtake can summarize visual review without rerunning capture or compare.

passed.description: True when this compare check passed within its configured threshold.

diff_path.description: Path to the diff/report artifact for this check when one was written.

screenshot_path.description: Path to the captured Storybook screenshot used in the compare.

reference_path.description: Path to the reference screenshot used in the compare.

diff_percent.description: Measured visual deviation ratio for this check when available.

severity.description: Deterministic severity from the compare-images CLI, derived from pixel ratio, spatial extent, and dimension drift together. Carried onto the artifact so outtake scores by severity, not pixel ratio alone — a small but widely-spread shift (low diff_percent, high extent) still lands as `major`/`critical` here.

VerifyResult.title: Verify Result
VerifyResult.description: One verify-capture run's measurement. `score` is the severity sum (critical×3 + major×2 + minor×1) over all checks — lower is better, 0 = perfect. Pixel diff and per-check breakdown sit alongside so callers see both structural and visual fidelity.

score.description: Σ(critical×3 + major×2 + minor×1) over all checks. 0 = perfect.

avg_diff_percent.description: Mean pixel deviation ratio across checks.

issues.description: Aggregate issue counts by severity over all checks.

checks.description: Per-check breakdown for an observed native view or an explicitly mapped responsive breakpoint.

view.description: Actual native view identity for an observation comparison.

tokens.description: This run's agent-reported LLM tokens. Best-effort; absent on headless runs.

ScoreReport.title: Score Report
ScoreReport.description: A design-verify run: first_shot (before any fix) and final (after the single verify-fix pass), each a full VerifyResult. delta = first_shot.score − final.score (positive = improvement; lower score is better).

tokens.description: LLM tokens summed across the capture + fix subagents. Best-effort.

Kind.title: Kind
Kind.description: The top-level render kind a `sync-verify` (and, by story input, a `sync-to`) run dispatches on, inferred from the story's Storybook group. `config` is an isolated single render (an `Entities/*` story) — within it a `selector`'s presence chooses the config-entity vs entity-view-mapping sub-mode. `scene` is a whole page (a `Designbook/Sections/*/Scenes` or `Designbook/Design System` story), captured full-page against the Scene's story. This binary is the single dispatch axis shared by both workflows. The Scene verification subject lives **here** — as the `scene` value of this enum — not in `#/ConfigType`, which stays scoped to the `config` branch.

ConfigType.title: Config Type
ConfigType.description: The kind of backend config subject on the `config` branch of a sync-verify run. `entity_view_display` is one display config verified against an isolated entity render. Not the dispatch axis — the top-level kind (`#/Kind`) is; this only names the config object type inside the `config` branch.

ConfigTarget.title: Config Target
ConfigTarget.description: The resolved subject of a `config`-kind sync-verify run — the backend config plus the two values derived from it: the Storybook story it maps to (the reference/baseline) and the backend render URL (the candidate). Backend-neutral: `config_id` is an opaque backend identifier; how it maps to a story and a URL is supplied per-config-type (core) and per-backend (integration), never hardcoded here.

config_id.description: Opaque backend subject identifier for this config_type. For `entity_view_display` this is the view-display id, `<entity_type>.<bundle>.<view_mode>`.

render_url.description: URL at which the backend renders the configured output, resolved by the `render_url` param resolver from a project-supplied command. The capture stage screenshots this URL as the candidate against the Storybook baseline.

StoryMeta.title: Story Meta
StoryMeta.description: On-disk `stories/{storyId}/meta.yml` — a thin binding from a story to a Reference. The reference owns the elements' states/breakpoints and the baseline; the story supplies its own per-element selector (and optional per-state steps on the story DOM).

states.description: Optional per-state story steps; when absent the reference's state names are reused with empty steps.

items.title: Capture Step
items.description: One generic browser interaction performed before a screenshot is taken, used to drive an element into a non-rest state. Source-agnostic — the same shape applies to a reference page or a Storybook story.

selector.description: CSS selector the action targets. Required for click/hover/focus; omitted for a bare wait.

timeout.description: Milliseconds to let the UI settle after the action.

component.description:
Bare component name — NO `provider:` namespace prefix (e.g. `hero`, `content_card`, `active-filters`; never `test_integration_drupal:hero`). Becomes the component directory and file basename (`components/<component>/<component>.component.yml`), so a namespace colon produces an invalid directory and breaks import resolution. The provider namespace is configured separately and is not part of this name.
A HYPHEN IS ALLOWED, and it was forbidden here by mistake until 2026-09-04. The colon is the hazard this pattern exists for; the hyphen ban was carried over from `Variant.id`, where it IS load-bearing because a variant id becomes a JS export name in the generated story (`mark-only` -> `export const Mark-only`, a SyntaxError). A component name becomes a directory, a file basename and a Storybook TITLE — never a JS identifier — so the same reasoning does not reach it.
Measured on 2026-09-04, against a theme shipping ten hyphenated components: Drupal's own SDC metadata schema admits `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`; `ComponentPluginManager` normalises nothing, so `gaia_theme:active-filters` resolves and `gaia_theme:active_filters` raises `ComponentNotFoundException`; and all sixteen stories of those ten rendered in a real browser with zero console errors. The old pattern therefore locked ten working components out of every workflow in this skill, with no defect to show for it.

id.description: Variant identifier in snake_case. Used as the story filename segment (`<component>.<id>.story.yml`) and as the key in `.component.yml` `variants:`. Hyphens are forbidden — the segment becomes a JS export name in the generated story (`mark-only` → `export const Mark-only`, a SyntaxError) and must satisfy the same identifier pattern as prop/slot keys.

title.description: Human-readable variant label shown in Storybook.

description.description: One-sentence summary of the variant's distinguishing visual or behavioural trait.

mode_kind.description: Which half of the bundle this mapping builds — `view` (reading half, written to entity-mapping/) or `form` (editing half, written to form-mapping/). Defaults to `view` so a caller that omits it (e.g. design-screen) is unchanged.

view_mode.description: View mode machine name; the mode name when mode_kind = view. Empty for a form mapping.

form_mode.description: Form mode machine name; the mode name when mode_kind = form. Empty for a view mapping.

DesignReference.title: Shared captured observations
DesignReference.description: Source and actual observations only. The design plan separately owns target structure, styling and implementation decisions.

subjects.description: Selected subjects, each with observations for its declared views and states.

parents.description: Observed ancestor layout dependencies; empty when none.

captures.description: Exact screenshot associations for selected subject, view and state cells.

fonts.description: Web fonts the reference renders text with. Each family that is not a Google/system font must be downloaded — see `files[]`. Metadata alone (family/weights) is insufficient: a self-hosted family with no `files[]` leaves downstream CSS with an unresolvable family and a silent serif fallback. This is the concrete failure mode `files[]` exists to prevent.

family.description: Exact font-family name as used in @font-face / CSS (e.g. "Reef", "Inter").

source.description: Where the font is served from. `self-hosted` and `adobe`/`other` families MUST be downloaded into `files[]`; `google` also needs local binaries for offline execution; `system` needs no download.

files.description: Downloaded font binaries for this family. Required when `source` is not `system`; frozen packages require offline binaries. Empty only when the font could not be downloaded.

src_url.description: Resolved absolute URL the binary was downloaded from.

local_path.description: Path (relative to the reference folder, typically under `{assets_dir}/fonts/`) where the binary was written.

images.description: Static images and brand assets detected in the design reference (logos, icons, illustrations).

reference_path.description: Downloaded asset path relative to the reference folder. Required by offline packages that reference this image's exact url identity; distinct from its public local_path URL.

url.description: Source URL or path of the image.

alt.description: Alt text or accessible label if present.

location.description: Where the image appears: header, footer, main, sidebar.

local_path.description: Path (relative to the Storybook `public/` or configured static dir) where the asset has been downloaded. Empty if the asset could not be downloaded or is decorative-only. Scenes and components MUST reference this path (e.g. ``) instead of text placeholders when it is set.

DesignWorkflowOutput.title: Design Workflow Output
DesignWorkflowOutput.description: Design-workflow-specific outtake payload. It builds on the global `WorkflowOutput` contract defined in `designbook/workflow/schemas.yml` and adds compare-oriented fields so shell/screen workflows can archive visual quality information alongside generic run metrics.

success_rate.description: Computed deterministically from compare_artifacts (never an AI judgment): success_rate = 1 − max(effective_deviation) over all artifacts, clamped to [0, 1]. Per artifact, effective_deviation = max(diff_percent, severity_floor[severity]) with floors pass→0.0, minor→0.05, major→0.20, critical→0.50, so the deterministic severity (pixel ratio + spatial extent + dimension drift) counts, not pixel ratio alone — a widely-spread shift with low diff_percent but severity major/critical still lowers the score. diff_percent and severity both come from the compare-images CLI, so identical screenshots yield the same score regardless of model. Edge cases: no design reference configured (reference_folder empty, no checks) → 1.0; a reference was set but compare_artifacts is empty (compare expected, produced nothing) → 0.0; an artifact missing diff_percent or severity, or an expected check absent from the matrix → effective_deviation 1.0 for that check (a failed measurement never raises the score). 0 = no match, 1 = perfect match. The summary derives flowRate from this value and recorded task attempts.

flow_rate.description: Composite-Score für den Research-Loop. Wird von der Summary deterministisch aus dem Laufzustand berechnet: flow_rate = success_rate * 100 - friction (errors*5 + retries*2 + unresolved*3). Wird nie vom AI geschrieben.

summary.description: Short human-readable outcome summary for the design workflow.

metrics.description: Prozessmetriken aus dem gespeicherten Laufzustand; die Summary berechnet sie.

compare_passed.description: True when the final visual comparison is considered passing for this workflow. This can remain false even when the workflow completed technically.

diff_path.description: Path to the final visual diff artifact when one was produced. Leave empty when no diff exists yet.

issues_count.description: Number of unresolved design issues considered by the outtake.

breakpoints_checked.description: Breakpoints covered by the final compare/review pass.

elements_checked.description: Elements covered by the final compare/review pass.

RegionProperties.title: Region Properties
RegionProperties.description:
Authoritative element properties for the region the current task covers.
Produced by the region-properties code resolver from the rendered DOM.
When `matched_via !== "none"`, `style` values are ground truth — markup
and CSS MUST use them where present. Falls back to the state's source dump
plus design hints only for properties not in the bag.

matched_via.description: Which heuristic located the region root.

root_id.description: ID of the region root inside `nodes`. Absent when matched_via === "none".

base_breakpoint.description: Smallest captured breakpoint — the mobile-first base for node `style`. Larger-breakpoint deltas live in each node's `overrides`. Absent for single-viewport captures.

nodes.description: All PropertyNodes in the region subtree. Hierarchy via parent_id / child_ids. Empty when matched_via === "none".

PropertyNode.title: Property Node
PropertyNode.description: One visible element from the captured source. Source-agnostic — a future Figma walker would return the same shape.

id.description: Deterministic node ID. Walker-chosen (DOM uses hash of dom_path + bbox).

parent_id.description: ID of this node's parent PropertyNode. Absent for the root — walkers MUST omit the key for the root node rather than emit null.

child_ids.description: Child node IDs in reading / visual order.

label.description: Human-readable name. Heading text, layer name, ARIA label, or text content.

kind.description: Coarse element category — drives consumer reasoning even when specific style fields are missing.

role.description: Normalized semantic role. Strong for DOM (HTML5 landmarks + ARIA). Optional.

heading_context.description: Nearest preceding section / heading text. The strongest source-agnostic anchor for region matching.

bbox.description: Pixel coordinates relative to the viewport.

text.description: Visible text content, trimmed, max 200 chars.

href.description: Absolute or root-relative URL for link nodes.

src.description: Asset URL or path for media nodes.

style.title: Curated Style
style.description: Source-agnostic curated style block. Walkers map their native properties (CSS computed style, Figma layout/fills/typography) onto this shape.

gap.description: Gap between flex / grid items, normalized in px.

background.description: Resolved hex color, or url() / image ref.

source.title: Source Locator
source.description: Walker-specific identification. `locator` is opaque to consumers; `raw` carries the unmapped native data when deep dives are needed.

locator.description: Walker-defined — DOM path for the URL walker.

raw.description: Walker-specific extra fields. Opaque to consumers — only loaded when explicitly requested. Keys vary by walker.

overrides.description: Per-breakpoint deviations from the mobile-first base. Each key is a breakpoint name (e.g. `sm`, `xl`); values list what changes at that breakpoint. Absent when the node is identical across breakpoints. Consume as responsive utilities: base `style` → base classes, `overrides.<bp>` → the matching `<bp>:` prefix.

hidden.description: Element not rendered at this breakpoint; `false` on a base-hidden node means it is revealed here.

style.description: Only the style properties that differ from the base `style` at this breakpoint.

bbox.description: Bounding box at this breakpoint when it differs from the base.

StorybookIndex.title: Refreshed Storybook entries
StorybookIndex.description: Actual index entries for the story IDs fixed during intake (derived CSF ids for written components plus exact live-index ids for retained stories), captured after the component build.

id.description: Story ID returned by the refreshed Storybook index.

items.description: Preserves the index entry fields supplied by Storybook, such as title, name and importPath.

StorybookChecks.title: Successful browser observations
StorybookChecks.description: Actual browser results and observations for the concrete stories, viewports and interactions fixed during intake.

result.description: Complete CHECK_RESULT returned by the browser check, including its measured diagnostics.

observations.description: Observed values keyed by the intake's declared appearance, behavior and responsive criteria, supported by browser logs or captures.

kind.description: Opaque source kind declared by its integration skill.

identity.description: Stable source identity supplied by the skill; may be a URL or file identity.

kind.description: Integration-defined locator kind such as css or figma-node.

value.description: Exact native identity; a Figma node is not a CSS selector.

id.description: Stable selected viewport or frame identity.

breakpoint.description: Explicit responsive mapping when established during intake.

states.description: Explicit observed states; source-specific replay details belong in the source workflow. Each state has its own dump `extract--<name>.json`, so a state name identifies one page load in one session across the whole revision and cannot carry different observers on different subjects.

session.description: Who observed this state. `anonymous` is the reserved name for a capture taken without a stored session; any other name must be a key of `sessions:` in designbook.config.yml, which resolves it to a Playwright storage state. Required so a published revision states its observer instead of defaulting to anonymous in silence.

views.description: Selected views; no implicit frame-to-breakpoint mapping.

path.description: Screenshot path relative to the CLI-owned revision directory.

ReferenceMaterial.title: Observed properties
ReferenceMaterial.description: Measured source values keyed by their native or normalized property names. Contains observed facts, not planned implementation decisions.

ReferenceStructure.title: Observed source structure
ReferenceStructure.description: Observed hierarchy with native locators. Target component structure belongs in the plan.

nodes.description: Reachable observed nodes; IDs and ordered children preserve source relationships.

kind.description: Observed native or normalized node category.

children.description: Ordered child node IDs, empty for leaves.

asset_ids.description: Exact images[].url identities required by this sample.

font_families.description: Exact fonts[].family identities required by this sample.

observations.description: Measured facts only; raw unmapped properties remain available for targeted inspection.

interactions.description: Observed interaction evidence; absent states are recorded as unavailable.

unavailable.description: Explicit observation gaps; a required gap blocks publication.

reason.description: Why the selected source cannot supply it.

required.description: Whether the agreed capture scope requires this information.

samples.description: One sample for each selected view and state; duplicate cells are invalid.

parent.description: Exact ancestor dependency identity when needed.

samples.description: Observed ancestor layout for the selected view and state.

CaptureFile.title: Captured binary artifact
CaptureFile.description: Declared direct screenshot or asset file; plan done records its exact file integrity.

reference.description: Absolute directory of the published revision.

subjects.description: Exactly one observed subject for this comparison.

states.description: Exactly one observed state for this comparison.

ObservationComparison.title: Explicit correspondence between captured source and actual observations

threshold.description: Maximum measured pixel deviation accepted by this check.

diff_path.description: Absolute planned path for the comparison diff outside either published revision.

ObservationCompareArtifact.title: Measured comparison of two published observation cells

passed.description: Measured diff is within the declared threshold and all evidence is valid.

reference_path.description: Exact source image path returned by the frozen query.

screenshot_path.description: Exact actual image path returned by the frozen query.
